subject: Coffee & Tea
title: What Is Oxidation?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is Oxidation?.

hook.text: Cut an apple and it turns brown. The same chemical process—oxidation—transforms tea leaves.

buildup.text: When tea leaves are bruised or rolled, enzymes react with oxygen, darkening the leaf and changing flavor.

discovery.text: Green tea is heated quickly to stop oxidation. Black tea is fully oxidized. Oolong stops somewhere between.

twist.text: Oxidation creates theaflavins and thearubigins—compounds that give black tea its amber color and malty taste.

climax.text: Controlling oxidation is the tea maker's core skill. Minutes of difference change the entire flavor profile.

punchline.text: Same leaf, different oxidation, different tea. Timing is flavor.

quiz.question: What chemical process distinguishes green tea from black tea?
